argument_summary: The certification case should be narrowed rather than overstated. On the current admissible record, aggregate readiness is supported by the overall pass margin and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance materials support documenting limitations and monitoring risk after launch. But that evidence does not erase the separate policy issue: the municipal permitting assistant segment is below target, is named in two city pilot commitments, and legal review remains open. The supportable position is therefore not clean compliance on the merits of the named-segment issue; it is a caveated certification packet that preserves the limitation explicitly and avoids treating documentation or monitoring as a substitute for the internal policy predicate.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost evidence is needed to resolve the audit treatment. The defensible governance move on this record is to avoid escalation to a stronger noncompliance conclusion if the packet is framed as caveated certification rather than clean certification.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts against any claim that the named-segment gap is immaterial merely because overall metrics passed or product labeled the segment non-core. The governing policy text says a weakness is material if it affects a named launch use case, and product labels do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in commitments or legal review is pending. The admissible record therefore supports, at most, a narrow aggregate-readiness rationale paired with explicit preservation of the unresolved named-segment limitation. It does not support a clean statement that policy has been fully satisfied without caveat.
concessions: Aggregate pass status and no severity-one rehearsal incidents do not by themselves satisfy the policy question for the named municipal permitting segment.
Public guidance on model cards and AI risk management supports disclosure and monitoring, but does not function as an internal waiver or approval.
The municipal permitting assistant segment remains below target, is named in two city pilot commitments, and legal review on disclosure is still open.
There is no admissible evidence here of an approved exception, waiver, or final legal determination permitting an uncaveated certification.
